status.note: the author's envelope and harness only; engines: Chromium 153 (headless shell), Firefox 155, WebKit 26.6 (Playwright builds, Linux)

what: Differences between browser engines that the web envelope (SPEC-TRAVEL 13.2) met, each with a page built so that the difference cannot arise, the naive construction that shows it, and the rule that makes it impossible. A reader or exporter passes an entry when its page gives the result stated in every engine.
how: Each page writes its verdict to <html data-result>: "pass", or "fail: " and why; it counts violations of its own policy. `where` says how it is opened: from a local file, from an http origin, or both. `drive` is real input for the runner to give, in order: focus and click (a selector), caret (a selection in the focused text box, in UTF-16 units), type, insertText, press (a key). `expect.requests` is how many requests the origin may see; `expect.download` a file that must come down. `naive[].fails` says, by engine, what goes wrong with the naive page; an engine not named there passes it. Entry 00 has no page: its subject is the envelope itself.

entries.name: The envelope as built: opened, edited by the keyboard, saved and reopened under its own policy
entries.rule: A web envelope, through opening, every face, an edit, saving and reopening what was saved, MUST cause zero policy violations, write nothing to the console, and make no request but the one that fetched it.
entries.pass: built by spike/envelope/make.mjs from vectors/compose.ufx and served from an http origin: by the keyboard alone: Tab to Edit, Enter; Tab to the field for the name, Enter, typing, Done (no dialog of the browser is shown at any point: one would fail the entry); Tab to a paragraph, Enter, typing, Done; back to Save, Enter, which shows what will leave; the copy with its history chosen, then "Save this copy": one file comes down; it reopens at the same state; over both pages zero securitypolicyviolation events, zero console messages, and the server saw each page asked for once and nothing else

entries.name: An engine asks the origin for an icon the page never named, and the page's own policy then reports the engine's request

fails.firefox: from http: GET /favicon.ico is attempted, blocked by default-src 'none', reported as an img-src violation and a console error

fails.chromium: console error: loading data:, violates default-src 'none'
fails.firefox: img-src violation and console error for data:,

entries.rule: A web envelope MUST name its icon itself, as an empty data: address (<link rel="icon" href="data:,">), and its policy MUST allow images from data: and from nowhere else (img-src data:). No engine then has a reason to ask any origin for anything.
entries.pass: opened from a local file and from an http origin: the server sees exactly one request (the page); zero securitypolicyviolation events; zero console messages

entries.name: A style written at run time (a style attribute, a style element made by script) is outside what a policy of hashes states, and is refused

fails.chromium: style-src-attr and style-src-elem violations; the style is not applied
fails.webkit: the same ("Refused to apply a stylesheet…")

fails.chromium: a style-src-attr violation; the node is not placed

entries.rule: Every byte a web envelope's policy constrains MUST be a part whose hash the envelope function writes into the policy: one style, one script. A binding MUST NOT write a style by any means (no style attribute, no style element, no style-sheet interface, no style property), with one exception: it places each accessible node over what is drawn for it by assigning, through the element's style object (the CSSOM) and in no other way, exactly the four properties left, top, width and height. Everything else about how those elements look (that they are positioned, transparent, what takes a pointer) and everything about how the rest of the page looks is stated by the hashed style sheet, and changed only by attributes (hidden, class, width, height, rows, ARIA) whose effect it states.
entries.pass: the changes take effect (computed style, size and the node's rectangle checked by the page); zero securitypolicyviolation events; zero console messages, from a file and from http, with style-src one hash and no unsafe-inline or unsafe-hashes. On the envelope itself: a static allow-list on the script as written and as shipped (the word style appears only in the query for the page's parts, in the canvas paints fillStyle and strokeStyle, and in assignments of .style.left, .style.top, .style.width, .style.height), and zero violations over open, every face, edits by keyboard and pointer, the Save panel, saving and reopening (entry 00, and test.mjs in every context)
entries.note: Setting a style property through script (element.style.left = …) is allowed under a hash-only style policy by all three engines here: the policy governs style attributes and style elements, not the CSSOM. The rule forbids it all the same, but for the four properties that place an accessible node over what is drawn for it, so that what the page may look like is still what the hashed style part says and only where a node lies comes from the drawing. Without that exception the nodes have no geometry, and touch exploration by a screen reader cannot land on what is drawn.

entries.name: A saved file that says it is a page may be opened as one, under the saving page's policy, where download is not honoured
entries.rule: A binding hands a file to the person as bytes of no declared kind (application/octet-stream), by a link with download that is never put into the page. It MUST NOT open, show or navigate to what it saves, so that no document but the envelope itself ever has to satisfy the envelope's policy.
entries.pass: from a local file and from an http origin: a download named as asked whose bytes are those given; the page's address does not change; zero violations; zero console messages; the server sees one request
entries.note: No engine here misbehaved with the naive construction. The rule is kept because the failure it prevents (the saved page shown in place, as a blob: document that inherits the policy) needs no bug, only a browser that ignores the download attribute.

entries.name: Engines say differently where a text box was changed: none gives target ranges for it, and after an undo WebKit leaves the restored text selected

fails.webkit: after undo the selection is the restored text (start 17, end 20), not a caret after it: the report says nothing was inserted, and the model no longer matches the text

fails.chromium: getTargetRanges() is an empty list for a textarea

entries.rule: A binding reports each change of an editing surface as (at, removed, inserted) only when the selection before and after accounts for it exactly: the text before `at` and after the change is unchanged. Otherwise it reports the whole text with no position, and it always reports the whole text when the entry ends. A kernel MUST accept both, and settle any disagreement by the whole text.
entries.pass: after typing, replacing a selection, Backspace, Delete, copy and paste, cut, delete-word, undo, text inserted by an input method, a line break and characters outside the basic plane: the reports, applied in order, give exactly the text the box holds
entries.note: Seen here: beforeinput and input fire for a textarea in all three with the same inputType values; getTargetRanges() is empty in all three; Firefox sends compositionend before the last input of a composition, the others after; WebKit selects what an undo restores.

entries.name: A touch on something that cannot be pressed, close to something that can: WebKit gives the click to the neighbour, at a point on the neighbour

fails.webkit: the click goes to the element with role button and tabindex above the line touched, and its clientX and clientY are a point on that element, not where the touch was

entries.rule: A binding takes where a pointer pressed from the pointer itself: the drawing it went down on, and the point it came up at (pointerdown, then pointerup within a few pixels, no pointercancel between). The click that follows says only that the press is complete: its target and its point are not used, since an engine may move them to a neighbouring control; and where it was moved to something outside the drawing, it is stopped there. A click that no pointer event came before (one made for the person by assistive technology or by script) names an element and no trustworthy point: it is a press on the node that element stands for.
entries.pass: a real touch on a paragraph, 11 pixels under a focusable element with role button that lies in it: exactly one press is taken, on the paragraph, at the point touched; zero violations; zero console messages
entries.note: Found when the accessible nodes were laid over the drawing (TRAVEL E23, the exception): until then the page held nothing a touch could be given to but the canvas. The piece of a button that was drawn on a second line had no element over it, and a tap on it was delivered as a click on the button above. In WebKit 26.6 as Playwright builds it for Linux; whether Safari on iOS does the same was not observed, but iOS is where this adjustment of touches is known from.

entries.name: The element that holds the focus is removed: Chromium reports the focus lost from inside the removal, and what the handler does breaks what the binding was doing

fails.chromium: NotFoundError from insertBefore: the node to be removed is no longer a child of this node

entries.rule: A binding handles one input event at a time. What the kernel asks for in answer to an event is done to the end before the next event is given to the kernel; an event that arrives meanwhile, from inside something the binding is doing, waits its turn.
entries.pass: the element holding the focus is removed and a new one placed before its sibling, while a listener answers a lost focus by removing that sibling: no error; zero violations; zero console messages
entries.note: Found when a decision was recorded through the tools (SPEC 5.4): a pressed word held the focus, the list of changes grew by a line, and the host removed the word's node. In Chromium 153. Firefox 155 and WebKit 26.6 do not report the focus lost at that moment.

harness.name: Playwright's screenshot puts a style element into the page; in WebKit the page's policy refuses it and reports it

seen.webkit: one style-src-elem violation and a console error for each screenshot

harness.rule: A conformance run takes no picture of a page it is asserting on, and puts nothing into it. What is observed of a page is observed from outside it, or by a script added before the page's own by means its policy does not govern.

harness.name: Request interception does not report the reading of a local file in Firefox

seen.chromium: the file:// address is reported once
seen.webkit: the file:// address is reported once

harness.rule: That nothing leaves a page is asserted by what every engine shows: the origin's own record of requests, the page's record of what it fetched (resource timing), and its policy violations. A count from the test tool's interception is "at most the page itself".
